notes.title: Post Trauma's first update, and a big thank you.
notes.content:
[h1]Post Trauma patch 1.05[/h1]


Hello there!
Thank you everyone for all the amazing support you showed for the game, it has been amazing seeing how people from all over the world played the game.

This is the first update, more things will come. So please continue to share your feedback because it helps me a lot!

If you liked the game and did not leave a review please do it! It helps A LOT to boost the visibility of the game at the Steam store. 

The patch will also be rolling out to consoles over the next two days. 

Thanks again! ❤️
-Roberto


[h2]Gameplay changes:[/h2]

[list]
[*] Updated Roman's movement so turning feels less sluggish.
[*] Added the option to use Tank Controls. (Any feedback on this is greatly appreciated).
[*] Added a new attack animation for the spear and made the current one a little bit faster.
[*] Added new enemy spawns.
[*] In hard mode now there are more empty tapes to pick up and I improved the visibility of all tapes so they are easier to see.
[*] Reworked how the dynamic loot system works. Ammo now has a higher chance to spawn and it's less likely to find two drawers with the same loot. If you have no med kits at all (chest included), the chance of finding a med kit will be higher.
[*] Allowed people to go back to the second save point in Act IV (the one before the stairs going up).
[/list]

[h2]Bugfixes[/h2]

[list]
[*] Fixed a bug that was causing the player to run even if they were not holding down the run button. [i](A feature for toggle run instead of hold is planned for the next patch)[/i]
[*] Fixed an issue that was forcing players to click "Resume game" at the save game menu instead of allowing them to use the back button shortcut.
[*] Now if you have the Y axis inverted the flashlight will also reflect the change not only the camera.
[*] Fixed an issue that was allowing the UI to show during cutscenes.
[*] Fixed the text at the mix samples machine in the hospital not reflecting introduced items after reloading a save.
[*] Fixed an issue that was causing the equipped weapon icon not being updated for some players.
[*] Fixed gun clipping issues at the prologue cutscene.
[*] Fixed an issue that was affecting Roman's moustache making it look brighter than intended.
[*] Fixed an issue that was causing the clothes of the king to flicker for some players.
[*] Fixed mop bucket physics so the player is unable to climb on top of them.
[*] Fixed "You are here indicator" at one of the school maps.
[*] Fixed an issue that was causing the model of one monster to not disappear after being killed in a cutscene and reloading the game.
[*] Adjusted the interaction trigger for giving the salts to Roman.
[*] Adjusted collisions in some levels.
[*] Minor stability improvements.
[/list]

notes.title: One Week To Go: The Team and Inspiration behind Post Trauma
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

With just one week to go until the launch of Post Trauma, we're celebrating the countdown to launch with several News Posts to answer some of your burning questions about the game, putting them to the creator, Roberto Serra of Red Soul Games.

Today, we're asking what was the inspiration behind the game, how long it's been in development, who's been working on it, and the games that left the biggest impression on Roberto.

Not long left to go - Don't forget to Wishlist Post Trauma if you haven't already and prepare for release on April 22!

[previewyoutube=Z1R-KKmX55I;full][/previewyoutube]

//////////////

[h2][b]What Inspired You To Make Post Trauma[/b][/h2]

To be honest, I started the development of Post Trauma as something  “just for fun” - At the time I was working at another indie studio, but I always wanted to do something of my own. I posted some screenshots on Twitter/X and to my surprise, the game got a lot of love. So I decided to quit my job and focus solely on Post Trauma.

I have always been a fan of old horror games, more slow paced with a big focus on puzzles and atmosphere over action scenes or big jumpscares. And as a hybrid developer - between an artist and a programmer - fixed cameras were the perfect excuse to make beautiful shots of any scene. I'm the type of player that, if given a good photo mode, will spend more time taking screenshots than actually playing. And in my personal opinion, fixed cameras can really work in favour of the horror aspects of the game.

[h2][b]How big is the team at Red Soul Games?[/b][/h2]
When people ask me how big the team at Red Soul Games is, I never know how to answer in a short sentence. So now that I have time, I will give you a long one.

Post Trauma started as a solo dev game. If you don't know me, my name is Roberto Serra and I used to work as a tech artist at Digital Sun Games (Moonlighter, Cataclismo, The Mageseeker: A League of Legends Story). 

Being a tech artist allowed me to write basic code and do a lot of the art on my own. There’s a lot of store bought assets that I had to adapt to fit into the style of the game, but of course I needed help if I wanted to finish the game.

Two months after signing with Raw Fury, in June of 2022, [url=https://www.artstation.com/pujadas]Pau Pujadas[/url] joined the team as a concept artist/art director. He is incredibly talented and elevated all the weird stuff I had in mind for the game times 10. I wish we could have included all the crazy concept art he did because some of that stuff is breathtaking. Pau's strongest skill is 2D art, but he also adapted really fast and was able to produce some amazing sculptures and organic fleshy monstrosities. And thanks to Unreal Engine 5’s Nanite, we could use optimized versions of those sculptures for the environments.

For the story I had a rough idea of the events that should happen in the game but I did not know how to develop the character or what to do with the world background. That’s why we contacted [url=https://www.cameronsuey.com/]Cameron Suey[/url] to help us with that. I gave him some documents with vague ideas and story events and after a few calls he was able to produce an amazing world with great characters and well written dialogues. So although he is not a member of the Red Soul Games team, his contribution was very important to Post Trauma.

In February of 2023, almost a year into development,[url=https://www.artstation.com/ingfrith] Andrés Montalvo[/url] joined the team as a 3D artist. He was a much-needed addition to the team, as Andrés was able to create actual good geometry for our game, and able to translate the 2D created concepts that Pau did, into amazing 3D models. He even designed some other great models on their own.

In July of 2023, we finally got an animator and [url=https://bsky.app/profile/alonsoanim.bsky.social]Javier Alonso[/url] was able to animate our characters and creatures the way we wanted, up until that point we were using a mix of premade animations and procedural ones.

In the last year of development, a good friend of mine joined the team [url=https://sites.google.com/view/lopezpefdev/home?authuser=0]Francisco López[/url], an Unreal Engine 5 developer, who helped me focus on other aspects of the game while he took care of the bigger programming tasks.

And not too long after him, [url=https://luismonrocle.com/]Luis Monrocle[/url], joined the team as audio designer. His work on the sound design of the game elevated the quality so much and made everything sound cohesive and oppressive. 

Not to mention our fantastic composer, [url=https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCiSKnkKCKAQVxMUWpZQobuQ]Nicolas Gasparini (Myuu)[/url] but we'll talk more about his work in another post! 
 
That’s it. Of course, the credit list is way longer because we had help from a lot of amazing people from other companies. But the peak of simultaneous people working full time on the project was 5 people. And for most time during development, we were just 3 people working full time on Post Trauma.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41489631/5c8b8b7a051418aa97e70eb2f863349f4feb0e17.jpg[/img]

[b][h2]What is the most important thing to understand about Post Trauma?[/h2][/b]

This is a very small, indie team - working on a game for three years - who have just tried their best to recreate something that looks like it fits on today’s market. We love these games just as much as you and with Post Trauma, we’ve tried to find a sweet spot that, we think, fans will appreciate. I think it’s important to recognise that this is a homage and a love letter to classic PS1/PS2 Survival Horror Games but we're just using modern day processing power and graphics to tell that story.

Modern horror games are quite different now - and that is a good thing - but sometimes I miss the feel older games offer. Post Trauma has been designed to feel like those older horror games, offering that alternative perspective we feel has been missing on the market for some time, and I hope you recognise that vibe immediately.  

And just like those classic games, Post Trauma will not handhold you too much. The puzzles require some thinking but they are not impossible and will hopefully feel rewarding. The combat is simple - and there will be some jank here and there - but hopefully it's good enough that you will feel the tension, think about every item in your inventory and spend time thinking about your progress. Maybe even be a little bit afraid of dying and losing progress because you forgot to use the radio to save the game. 

Or perhaps you will decide to restart a save on purpose because you accidentally used a shotgun shell on a weak enemy, realising that those are actually quite hard to find.

There will be puzzles, a lot of them, and you probably will need a pen and paper to help solve them. And while there is combat, the aim of the game is to build atmosphere through music, story-telling, setting a scene and making The Gloom and the environments Roman finds himself in incredibly distinct and unsettling. 

This is classic survival horror re-imagined, but still a puzzle first experience. Our small team has done everything possible to try and bring this style back with a modern day feel.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41489631/6e71c7a8c44d8887604571645e5882a65f6d591b.jpg[/img]

[h2][b]Which games left the biggest impression on you?[/b][/h2]

A lot of them! It’s hard to pick. 

My favourite game of all time is The Legend of Zelda, Majora’s Mask (The N64 version, not the more recent 3DS edition). The different ways characters in that game deal with their inevitable death was very interesting to me. 

Silent Hill, of course, is a big inspiration. My favourite one is 4 and I really like how that game mixes fixed cameras with first person. But also after a few hours the game corrupts even your “safe place”.

However, I must say my favourite horror game is Dead Space! Post Trauma might have taken inspiration from all of those, because, even if I'm not adding those references on purpose, maybe my subconscious has because of all the games that I've played in the past.

[h2][b]How long has Post Trauma been in development?[/b][/h2]

The actual development has been exactly three years. I signed a contract with Raw Fury in April of 2022 which allowed me to restart the development.

Before that, all I had was a vague idea of what the game would be and a demo, which was made in a few months and somehow held together with duct tape and dreams.

But that initial demo got a strong reception, and not long after I signed with Raw Fury, we reannounced the game at The Game Awards. We’ve been building to this moment ever since.

It’s exciting, scary, daunting, and there’s been a few bumps in the road, but we’re[b] excited for everyone to finally play the game on April 22![/b]

See you in the Gloom

Roberto

notes.title: Post Trauma will now release on April 22
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

We want to extend our gratitude and thanks for your continued support of Post Trauma.

As a very small team, your input continues to be invaluable and we deeply appreciate all of your comments over the course of development.

However, due to some unfortunate, unexpected circumstances, we need to push the release of Post Trauma back by a few weeks. 

The [b]new and final release date is April 22nd, 2025 across PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.[/b]

We can also confirm the price point of the game will be [b]$14.99 / €14.99.[/b]

This is not the position we want to be in so close to our previously intended release date and recognise the game's development journey has been tricky to navigate; be assured we don't take this decision lightly. We're incredibly sorry for any disappointment or frustration this announcement causes.

Thank you for continued patience, we look forward to welcoming you to The Gloom on April 22nd, whether you're playing on PC, PlayStation 5, or Xbox Series X|S.

- Raw Fury and Red Soul Games

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41489631/f916ce4ffb4a6a2549f49c5cea48780bf0a0310e.png[/img]

notes.title: February 2025 Update: Steam Next Fest!
notes.content:
Hello

Hope you’re having a great 2025 so far. Thanks for all of your support last year!

We just wanted to let you know that development is proceeding well on Post Trauma and we’re all working really hard to make something truly special. We’re not quite ready to talk release date just yet but we will have some exciting news and updates to share in the coming weeks.

For now, what we can tell you is that Post Trauma will be in this months’ Steam Next Fest! That’s right, you’ll soon be able to check out a playable slice of the game and enter The Gloom for yourself.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41489631/b94eccee74282a32cf9630228b01c212dd013e61.png[/img]

This is a huge moment for us. While we’ve been fortunate to be able to take Post Trauma around the world, from Gamescom to Tokyo Game Show, our goal has always been to share the horror with as many people as possible and this feels like the perfect time for you to see what we’ve been up to. 

We cannot wait to hear what you think of Post Trauma and look forward to providing more details on what to expect ahead of the demo’s release. Make sure to stay Wishlisted right here to get all the latest updates. Thanks for all of your support! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41489631/695e2157ce9bcc60d6034df1dee3f50ffe649f3a.jpg[/img]

See you in The Gloom very soon!

Roberto

notes.title: August 2024 Update: Release Date, New Music and Fantastic Games
notes.content:
Hello!

In case you missed the big news last week, we've announced our release date! Post Trauma will officially launch on Steam on October 29th 2024, just in time for Halloween!

[previewyoutube=Tb9EwFKEi28;full][/previewyoutube]

This is an enormous moment for us and one we're incredibly excited about. There's still a lot of work to do between now and then, of course, but it won't be too much longer before you're able to play Post Trauma for yourselves!

In our latest trailer, you get a new look at the Metro Station, an area that will be familiar to those who played the original demo on Itch. As you can see, it's come a long way since then but that's just the start.

You'll also get a look at some of the creatures you'll face, areas you'll visit and other characters you'll meet. We'll talk more about all of that in the coming weeks between now and release.

Perhaps the biggest thing you'll have noticed is the title track for Post Trauma, composed by Nicolas Gasparini (Myuu) playing in the background. We're all thrilled you're now getting a chance to hear the music for Post Trauma and it's but a taste of what to expect when the full game rolls around. 

[h2][b]Fantastic Games 2024[/b][/h2]

As if that's not enough, it's just been announced that we'll be at Fantastic Games 2024 this September.  In this first ever event, the sickest and most spine-tingling upcoming sci-fi, horror and fantasy indie games will be showcased in Austin, Texas, presented by Day of the Devs!

From September 20th till September 22nd, players will be able to check out Post Trauma alongside some other fantastic horror titles in an event sponsored by the likes of Blumhouse Games, Devolver and Raw Fury.

It's an incredible opportunity and we're so grateful for the chance to connect with the community, but are even more excited for new players to dive into Post Trauma.

And that's not all! Stay tuned, as we've got a lot more to talk about in the weeks and months ahead, so make sure to Wishlist Post Trauma and tell your friends to do the same!

See you in the Gloom.

Roberto

notes.title: May 2024 Update: Release Window Adjustment and more!
notes.content:
Hello there! 

It’s been a while, hope everyone is doing well! As you may have recently seen, we were featured during the Guerilla Collective with an all-new trailer for Post Trauma! And in case you missed it, you can watch it here!

[previewyoutube=f_Sqvd8UCfE;full][/previewyoutube]

You may have noticed our release window has changed. We were originally targeting Spring 2024 but as development progressed, we realised we needed a bit more time to make Post Trauma the best game it can be so we’ll now be launching [b]Fall 2024[/b]. I trust you will understand and can forgive us for the short delay! 💔

Hopefully you can already see the progress from our latest trailer which includes a look at some cutscenes, as well as updates to character likeness, game mood, lighting effects, and more.

The trailer also shows off the voice acting talent in the game for the first time, including Togo Igawa as Roman, but also the brilliant Autumn Ivy and Hyoie O’Grady. We’re excited to share more about the cast of Post Trauma in future updates, but let’s just say Roman isn’t the only one trying to survive in this terrifying, twisted place.

You may have also seen that we announced some additional platforms for Post Trauma. We’re really excited to be able to invite more players into The Gloom and we will share more news about this in the coming weeks.

Speaking of, some members of the press were able to get new hands on with Post Trauma at a recent press event in the Raw Fury offices. And we’ve seen some amazing coverage from the likes of [url=https://www.eurogamer.net/post-trauma-is-a-survival-horror-that-stubbornly-refuses-to-give-you-any-answers-and-i-like-that-a-lot]Eurogamer[/url] and [url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/post-trauma/impressions]PCGamesN[/url], and it seems they really liked the game!. We’re so delighted to see the response and grateful for the kind words.🖤

I want to thank you again for your patience and continued support of Post Trauma, we appreciate each and every one of you. You definitely won’t have to wait so long for an update from us as there’s a lot more to come in the next few months. Keep speculating on the trailer, let us know what you think about the progress, and be sure to wishlist us, share and shout about the game as much as you can. It helps massively.

Have a wonderful day!

Roberto

notes.title: August 2023 update : Release window announcement and more!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

 

I hope you are doing great. I am doing super great! We just got featured on the Gamescom Opening Night Live, this is the second time Geoff Keighley has given us the chance to share Post Trauma with the world I can can't say thank you for it enough times.


Thank you to all the people that have been there from the beginning, thank you to the people that got here from the Game Awards and thank you to all the new people that just got here! Please remember to wishlist the game if you can, it's a free and easy way to help us out!

 

There's a lot of stuff I want to talk about, so I'll start with this. What did you think of the trailer?! I really hope you liked it, we tried to tease a lot of stuff without spoiling anything from the story. Where's Roman? What are those creatures? Is that the same spider lady from the original demo? And who is that woman on the speaker?!? I know all the answers but you will have to wait until the game's out .

 

And speaking of when the game is out... We just announced that the game will come out SPRING 2024! That might sound super far away but trust me, in game development it's just the blink of an eye. Though the team has grown a little since the last time, we are still suuuper small, so a lot of those extra hands will be working to make sure the quality of the final game will be awesome.

 

This week at Gamescom journalists will be able to get a glimpse of the game, it's the first time we are letting several people try the game this way since we released the original demo, so I can't wait to read what they think! I hope they will enjoy playing it as much as we enjoyed creating it.

 

I really don't know what else to say besides THANK YOU for supporting the game and making the dream of this indie dev become true!

 

I hope you have a great day and I will see you all in The Gloom.


Roberto

notes.title: December 2022 update - Partnership announcement & more
notes.content:
Okay, I have a lot of things to tell you, A lot!! And I don't know where to start so I guess I'll start by thanking you.

Thank you!! Thank you everyone for your patience with me!

I can finally tell you that a few months ago I founded an indie studio named Red Soul Games and for the past few months we have been working with Raw Fury on Post Trauma.

This is wonderful news for the development of the game, but I want to make it clear that working with Raw Fury won't make Post Trauma a bigger game than the one I had in mind when I released the demo. It means that the game will receive a lot more love..

Thanks to RF I can now have a lot of things that I couldn't take care of on my own or that a publisher does better than me. It also allows me to bring new people to the team like for example Pau Pujadas, who is helping me A LOT with the art of the game.

I apologize for the lack of updates so far, I have been focusing 100% on the development of the game and I must confess that interacting on social networks gives me some anxiety, sorry if I missed some DMs! I would like to introduce you to Elena, Alexandre and Gemma, who will help me a bit with PR, marketing and social networks. I will still be there! But with their help, I will be allowed to focus on the game as well as keeping you updated on how the development is going.

For now I can confirm that the game will be released on consoles as well as PC, it was always the intention but now I have help to make it happen! I will share more information about that soon.

In case some of you don't know what this is all about, it's because yesterday we announced Post Trauma at The Game Awards, thanks to Geoff Keighley and the team behind The Game Awards for giving me the opportunity to share Post Trauma with a lot of new people. Go watch the announcement trailer if you haven't! LINK

I honestly don't know what to say, I'm still afraid to wake up one day and realize I was dreaming. A little over a year ago I left a stable job to dedicate myself completely to a demo and now I can live from it? Impossible, this must be a lucid dream.

Many thanks to HorrorVisuals, and especially to all of you who shared the Post Trauma Demo with the world, without you this would not have been possible. <3 

And to all of you who have just met Post Trauma, WELCOME! 

Have a wonderful day!
-Roberto
